ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The mode of neural innervation received by the human heart and adrenal gland is shown in the figure. Answer the question: What regulatory mode regulates cardiovascular activity through pathway B?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The right side of the figure is labeled pathway B, showing nerve fibers from the nerve center reaching the adrenal gland; beside the adrenal gland is labeled “adrenaline,” and arrows indicate adrenaline entering the blood and then acting on the heart and blood vessels. Reasoning: The first half of pathway B is the nerve center controlling the adrenal gland through nerves, which belongs to neural regulation; the second half is the adrenal gland releasing adrenaline, which is transported through the blood and acts on the cardiovascular system, which belongs to humoral regulation. Therefore the mode of regulating cardiovascular activity through pathway B is the joint participation of neural regulation and humoral regulation, namely neuro-humoral regulation.
